newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Late selling pulls Taiwan stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Late selling pulls Taiwan stocks to lower close.

text.p: Late waves of profit-taking against strong recent gains pulled Taiwan share prices a lower close and brokers said the market was likely to undergo a correction before resuming a bull run begun in mid-November.
The weighted index, after spiking up 101 points, reversed swiftly in late trade to end 46.42 points or 0.66 percent lower at 6,936.39. Turnover was a very heavy T$125.9 billion.
Despite a bullish mood, brokers said a correction was needed after November's rally and further sharp gains since Saturday.
"Profit-taking was very heavy before the close and that may continue tomorrow," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
Monday's rise and Tuesday's mid-morning peak suggested a return of November's bull run but the highs were unsustainable.
Financial shares, which had driven mid-morning sentiment, also were hit by profit-taking, losing 0.54 percent.
The financials surge was seen as a belated welcome after the Chicago Mercantile Exchange received U.S. regulatory approval on November 27 to launch Taiwan stock-index futures contracts.
"Investors picked up the news...as an excuse to buy today," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities.
Despite the late downward correction, Taiwan's "big three" state-run banks nevertheless posted gains.
Hua Nan bank was up T$3 percent to T$129 and both Chang Hua bank and First bank gained T$1 to T$156 and T$166 respectively.
"The market again failed to stay above the 7,000-point barrier and that means it will take some more time to break the resistance," said Lin of Golden Securities.
Some brokers noted continued year-end selling by foreign institutions but they agreed that the current loose liquidity at home would support the market.
Futures-related financials and big-capital shares were likely to remain the market focus in the near term, they said.
